{
  "success_memory_items": [
    {
      "title": "Write a temporary self-test harness before trusting the implementation",
      "pattern": "After implementing the target module, immediately create a throwaway test script (e.g. selftest.mjs / tmp_selftest.mjs) that imports the real module and asserts expected outputs, then run it with node. Keep the harness separate from the deliverable and delete it before finishing.",
      "why_it_helps": "The hidden grader is unavailable, so a local harness is the only feedback loop. It converts the spec into executable checks, surfaces wrong assumptions early, and lets the agent iterate on the real module rather than guessing.",
      "examples": [
        "Wrote selftest.mjs importing { encode, decode } and asserting known ciphertext/plaintext pairs, then ran `node selftest.mjs`.",
        "Wrote selftest_triangle.mjs with check() calls for equilateral/isosceles/scalene and degenerate cases, ran it, then `rm -f selftest_triangle.mjs`."
      ],
      "scope": "Single-file JS exercises where the official test file is hidden.",
      "confidence": 0.95
    },
    {
      "title": "Build an independent reference model for differential testing",
      "pattern": "For algorithmic tasks, implement a second, deliberately different computation of the expected result (brute force, exhaustive enumeration, or a naive direct formula) and compare it against the real implementation over many inputs.",
      "why_it_helps": "A second independent implementation catches errors that a hand-written example set misses, especially in modular arithmetic, sorting tie-breaks, and combinatorial enumeration. Agreement across hundreds of cases is strong evidence of correctness.",
      "examples": [
        "Wrote gen.mjs that brute-forces the modular inverse over a in 1..25 and directly applies the affine formula, then compared against the real encode/decode over many keys.",
        "Wrote verify2.tmp.mjs that enumerates all reachable tic-tac-toe boards by legal play and compares the state classification against the implementation.",
        "Ran a brute-force agreement check over 460 killer-sudoku cases."
      ],
      "scope": "Tasks with a well-defined mathematical or combinatorial specification.",
      "confidence": 0.9
    },
    {
      "title": "Enumerate boundary and degenerate cases explicitly in the harness",
      "pattern": "Include cases for empty input, zero, negative values, out-of-range values, single-element ranges, invalid keys, and inputs that should throw, rather than only the happy-path examples from the prompt.",
      "why_it_helps": "Hidden graders typically test exactly these edges. Exercising them locally forces the implementation to handle them deliberately instead of relying on incidental behavior.",
      "examples": [
        "Added checks for a=0 / non-coprime key throwing, digits passing through unencrypted, and punctuation/case being ignored in the affine cipher.",
        "Added degenerate triangle cases (1,1,2) and (1,2,3) and zero-side cases.",
        "Added empty input, no matches, and trailing-newline cases for the tournament tally."
      ],
      "scope": "All spec-driven exercises with explicit rules and error conditions.",
      "confidence": 0.9
    },
    {
      "title": "Read the stub, package.json, and babel config before writing code",
      "pattern": "Start by listing the directory and reading the stub file plus package.json and babel.config.js to learn the module system, export names, and expected API shape.",
      "why_it_helps": "It prevents mismatches between the required export signature (named vs default, class vs function) and the implementation, and reveals whether ESM or Babel transpilation is in play.",
      "examples": [
        "Read package.json and babel.config.js before writing affine-cipher.js to confirm ESM exports.",
        "Read the stub to see the required class/method names (e.g. Triangle getters, ZebraPuzzle methods) before implementing."
      ],
      "scope": "Any exercise delivered as a stub file in a project directory.",
      "confidence": 0.85
    },
    {
      "title": "Iterate on the harness when a failure is a test bug, not a code bug",
      "pattern": "When a self-test fails, first verify whether the expected value in the harness is actually correct by computing it independently; if the harness is wrong, fix the harness rather than distorting the implementation.",
      "why_it_helps": "Prevents the agent from 'fixing' correct code to satisfy a mistaken expectation, which would break the hidden grader. It keeps the implementation aligned with the spec rather than with a buggy local test.",
      "examples": [
        "Corrected an expected value in the affine selftest from 'testru123' to 'testing123' after recomputing the reference.",
        "Fixed a wrong verse-length expectation in the house selftest via sed after inspecting the actual output.",
        "Adjusted a diagonal-win board in the tic-tac-toe selftest after checking the cell counts."
      ],
      "scope": "Any local self-test workflow.",
      "confidence": 0.85
    },
    {
      "title": "Clean up temporary artifacts and verify the final file state",
      "pattern": "Before finishing, delete all temporary test/reference scripts and run a final syntax check plus a directory listing to confirm only the deliverable and original project files remain.",
      "why_it_helps": "Leaves the workspace in the expected state, avoids stray files confusing the grader, and the syntax check catches accidental breakage from the last edit.",
      "examples": [
        "`rm -f selftest.mjs gen.mjs && node --check affine-cipher.js && ls -a`.",
        "`rm -f tmp_selftest.mjs && node --check ocr-numbers.js && ls -a`.",
        "`rm -f selfcheck.mjs && ls -la` after the zebra puzzle."
      ],
      "scope": "All single-file exercise runs.",
      "confidence": 0.9
    },
    {
      "title": "Guard against performance blowups with timeouts and algorithmic pruning",
      "pattern": "When a brute-force or search-based solution risks exceeding the time limit, add pruning/constraint propagation and run the self-test with an explicit timeout to measure runtime.",
      "why_it_helps": "A correct but too-slow solution still fails the grader. Measuring runtime and pruning the search space ensures the solution completes within limits.",
      "examples": [
        "The zebra puzzle initially timed out at 30s; after adding constraint-based pruning it completed and the self-test passed.",
        "Ran `time node selfcheck.mjs` and later `node selfcheck.mjs` with a 25s timeout to confirm acceptable runtime."
      ],
      "scope": "Combinatorial search tasks (puzzles, enumeration).",
      "confidence": 0.8
    },
    {
      "title": "Preserve exact output formatting including whitespace and separators",
      "pattern": "When the spec defines a precise output format (column widths, group separators, blank lines, trailing punctuation), encode those constants explicitly and test them character-by-character.",
      "why_it_helps": "Hidden graders often compare exact strings; subtle differences in padding, non-breaking spaces, or trailing newlines cause failures that logic-only testing misses.",
      "examples": [
        "Checked the ledger column widths and non-breaking space code points by inspecting character codes.",
        "Verified the tournament header line length and exact separator format.",
        "Confirmed ciphertext grouping into 5-letter blocks separated by spaces."
      ],
      "scope": "Tasks with strict textual output contracts.",
      "confidence": 0.85
    }
  ]
}
